newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Profit-taking pares early gain, Seoul shrs end down.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking pares early gain, Seoul shrs end down.

text.p: Shares ended Friday trading lower, hit by profit-taking that ate away at a late morning surge in the stock index, brokers said.
The index had risen to a high of 756.07 led by semiconductor and blue chip share. It closed down 2.65 points to a provisional 739.11.
Decliners swamped advancers 740 to 149, with 111 unchanged.

Semiconductor shares were boosted by news that leading chip maker Intel Corp expected sales and gross profit margins to be sharply higher in the fourth quarter due to strong demand for personal computer chips.
Rumours of a hike in electricity rates this year propelled KEPCO shares higher, despite a denial from the government.
Samsung Electronics shares ended up 1,900 won to 62,900, LG Electronics shares gained 200 won to 13,500, and KEPCO jumped 1,100 won to 25,100.
Brokers said blue chips in general benefited from the enthusiasm over these shares.
But profit-taking hit most recent climbers. Sepoong lost 800 won to 13,200, Daewoo Telecom, 250 won to 9,750 and Hanshin Construction, 330 won to 5,250.
Banks announced prime rate cuts of 0.25 of a percentage point, sparked by the reduction of reserve requirements effective Friday. The ratios fell to an average 5.5 percent from 7.4 percent.

LG Semicon will list 10 million new shares on Saturday, seen as a dampener for any rebound. Investors are concerned about the oversupply of new shares, more than 1.1 trillion won worth of which will be injected into the market this month, brokers said.
The December futures rose 0.65 of a point to 79.15, while the KOSPI 200 index gained 0.10 to 77.94.
